newsitem.title: USA: U.S 10-yr notes seen in demand at upcoming auction.
newsitem.headline: U.S 10-yr notes seen in demand at upcoming auction.

text.p: The $10.0 billion in new 10-year notes that the U.S. Treasury plans to auction on Tuesday should attract a solid bid, analysts said.
"We think it's going to go ok," said Patrick Dimick, Treasury market analyst at CS First Boston.
"(An average yield) around 6.52 percent where it is now would be reasonable," he said. "The way the issue has traded this morning, we think it's going to go ok."
Analysts said there were rumors that Japanese buyers would participate in the auction.

"There's talk of Japanese investors selling German 10-years to buy U.S. 10-years," said Dimick. "The spread (between them) is very wide right now -- about 55 basis points -- between a 5.97 percent yield (for the German 10-year) and 6.52 percent on U.S. 10-year notes."
"The U.S. is the cheaper of the two issues so that trade might appeal to some investors," Dimick said.
The Treasury last sold 10-year notes on August 7 during its quarterly refinancing effort. The bid-to-cover ratio then was a weak 2.22 to one.
The last Treasury 10-year note auction that was not part of a three-part refunding cycle occurred on July 9. That sale drew a firmer bid, with the bid-to-cover ratio 2.66 to one.
The average yield at the August 7 auction was 6.535 percent, down from the average yield of 7.016 percent at the July 9 auction.
Josh Stiles, Treasury bond strategist at I.D.E.A., noted that the market is very close to the high end of its six-month trading range.

"You could see interest from mortgage players," said Stiles. "If there's a pickup in mortgage refinancing, the duration of their portfolios shortens and (managers) want to get back up to their benchmarks. So they're potential buyers of the 10-years."
As for Japanese investors, Stiles said there has been "good buying out of Japan in the 10-year sector recently."
Stiles said European bond markets "look tired," but added that there are not a lot of European fund managers willing to bet on a big breakout to the upside in the U.S. Treasury market.
Still, the size of the auction is a moderate $10.0 billion and that should help it get distributed, traders said.
Richard Koss, economist at Maria Fiorini Ramirez Inc, said "we've gotten sort of a golden tone around the market right now" that could help smooth the auction.
"The next employment report is a month away -- which looks like infinity to the market," said Koss. "There's probably enough bulls out there to do it," said Stiles.
The 10-year notes were yielding 6.515 percent in when-issued trade at 1140 EDT/1540 GMT. The deadline for bids is 1300 EDT/1700 GMT. Results are due about 1340 EDT/1740 GMT.
